root_cause.text: The code used the outdated config macro `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG` instead of the renamed `CONFIG_CFI`, causing the CFI enforcement logic for `btf_dtor_kfunc_t` to be compiled out entirely, thus failing to prevent type mismatch violations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG)` to `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI)` in `kernel/bpf/btf.c`. The commit message states: "Using the wrong name results in the code getting compiled out. Meaning the CFI failures for btf_dtor_kfunc_t would still trigger." This confirms that the bug exists due to the stale config reference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing CFI type validation for destructor kfuncs when using non-Clang CFI implementations by switching to the common CONFIG_CFI option.
intent_record.what: Changed the preprocessor conditional from IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG) to IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI) in the btf_check_dtor_kfuncs function.
intent_record.how: Broadens the type-checking logic for destructor kfuncs to be active when any CFI implementation is enabled (via the general CONFIG_CFI config), rather than only when Clang's specific CFI is enabled. This ensures the validation that the destructor kfunc type is void applies to both Clang and GCC CFI (or other implementations).
